_about: ENHANCEMENT E24: every translatable text's ROOM - how wide and how many lines it may be where the game draws it, on the 1024x768 logical screen (the 4:3 view; widescreen only adds room) - so a translation can use the room there is rather than the width of the Portuguese and English. test_pn_render_hud (TestRooms) lays every language's text out with the game's own FontAtlas and prints each line past its room: 'room <lang> "<key>" line N: <w> px > <max> px (<face> <size>)'. PN_ROOM_REPORT=<id> (or all) prints each entry's widest line against its room. Sections mirror strings.json: 'strings' and 'touch' by the Portuguese key, 'patterns' by the pattern's pt with a 'sample', the Portuguese as the script composes it, which the test translates. 'prefix' is drawn before the text on its line (a Switch row's '[x] ', the widest marker) and counts in its width. maxWidth is logical px per line from the text's anchor: to the next element on the same row, less a 10 px gap (to where that element is drawn: a sprite's box, a text's pen); to a panel's edge (showData's panel: from x 642 to the screen's right edge, 381 as the E16 and E21 checks measure it; the pause's panel and rows, less the inset they give the text on the left); or to the screen's right edge less a 30 px margin (the options screen's own margin), whichever comes first on the text's rows. maxLines comes from the height: showData's body is 25 px lines from y 70, 27 of them above 768; a text that shares the panel with another (the credits and E21's, the two Versus paragraphs, an arena and its unlock text) gets 27 less the other's lines in pt/en and the blank line between. rule 'visual': a text with no box to fill - world text (lore signs), the messages and help signs (one 30 px slot each), the arena descriptions - may be max(pt, en) x 1.15 wide and have their line count, measured with the stand-in faces (FontAtlas.hpp), and no wider than 'cap', its hard limit; the test recomputes these from strings.json, so a changed English shows as a stale room. maxWidth null: never drawn. Portuguese and English fit every room: one that does not is a wrong room, not a wrong text.
